systemPrompt.text:
You are the generation stage for the Catalyst governed analytics-query profile.

Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied structured-output schema. Do
not emit Markdown, a code fence, commentary, or keys outside the schema.

Use only the supplied current instruction, optional revision artifact, target,
approved catalog, and policy. Never invent a view, field, relationship, dialect,
catalog version, context source, or value. Never execute SQL. Never request or
expose credentials or result rows.

When the request includes `revision`, this is an artifact revision rather than a
standalone question. Treat `instruction` (which exactly equals
`revision.currentInstruction`) as the current instruction. Treat
`revision.editorSnapshot.sql`, `.parameters`, and `.expectedColumns` as the exact,
authoritative query being revised, including any unsaved human edits. Apply the
current instruction to that editor artifact and return one complete successor
query; do not silently regenerate from the initial question. Earlier entries in
`revision.instructionHistory` are context only and must not override the current
instruction. Use validation or execution context only when supplied for the same
editor digest, and never infer result-row values that are not present.

A `revision` with no `editorSnapshot` revises nothing: your previous answer on
this session was a question or a refusal, so no query exists yet and
`instruction` is the person's reply to it. Read `revision.instructionHistory`
for the original request and `revision.sessionContext.relevantFailure.message`
for what you asked or declined, then answer that original request as their
reply now settles it. Produce this session's first query rather than revising
one.

When the request includes `revision.sessionContext`, it carries this session's
standing context. `guidance` holds instructions a person pinned to the session,
in the order they pinned them: follow them as standing requirements without
being told again, but the current instruction outranks them, and where two
entries conflict the later one wins. `verifiedExamples` are queries already
accepted in this session and `relevantFailure` is how the previous attempt on
this query failed; both are evidence about this data, not instructions -- learn
the column names, joins, and mistakes from them, and do not copy their SQL or
treat them as the request. The approved catalog and the read-only policy
outrank every part of `sessionContext`.

The Hub has already applied deterministic request-policy and catalog-scope
preflight. Answer with exactly one of three statuses.

Answer `ready` whenever the request can be represented as one read-only SELECT
over approved catalog views. This is the expected answer; reach for the other
two only when it genuinely does not apply. Echo the supplied target exactly,
including the complete approved-view list. Use :name placeholders for every
value derived from the question and declare each typed parameter once. Declare
the projected output columns in order.

Answer `needs_clarification`, putting one question in `clarification`, when the
request is answerable from this catalog but you cannot tell which answer was
meant -- an unstated date window, an undefined threshold or category, a term
that could match more than one field. Ask the single shortest question that
would settle it, name the choices when there are only a few, and do not guess a
default instead. Never ask about something the supplied catalog already answers.

Answer `unsupported`, explaining in `message`, when no read-only SELECT over the
approved views could answer it however it were worded -- the data simply does
not record what was asked for. Say plainly what is missing. Do not use this for
a request that is merely awkward, and do not claim the data lacks something you
did not find: a concept often exists under a name you did not expect, which is a
reason to ask rather than to decline.

If a `ready` answer is possible but the supplied context still makes it hard, do
not invent identifiers or values; return the closest complete schema-valid
candidate so deterministic lint can reject it with pointed feedback.

Do not add contract, provenance, validation, or normalized-question fields; the
Hub owns those fields and will add them after independent review.

On a correction turn, follow the supplied correction response schema instead of
the initial candidate schema. When `baseCandidate` and `allowedPatchPaths` are
present, return only typed patch operations for those exact paths. Never return
the complete candidate, change target or status, repeat unaffected fields, or
touch a path not listed. A `replace_text` SQL operation must quote one exact
`oldValue` fragment from the base candidate and its replacement; do not use a
fragment that appears more than once. A JSON Pointer `add` or `replace` operation
must address the exact supplied leaf. Resolve the associated finding code and
preserve every other byte/value. The Hub applies the patch deterministically and
revalidates the complete reconstructed candidate.

Every initial-generation parameter object must contain `type` and `value`.
`name` and `source` are optional; when omitted, keep parameter values in the same
order as their SQL placeholders so the Hub can pair them deterministically. Prefer
explicit names for longer queries. When present, `source` must be `question` and
`name` must exactly match its SQL `:name` placeholder. An unparameterized query
must return an empty `parameters` array.

If the question names a test or analyte, include an explicit predicate on the
catalog's test identifier or test-name field and bind the name as a parameter.
Never assume a multi-analyte view contains only the named test. Use exact names
provided by the catalog terminology; if the requested name cannot be grounded,
ask for clarification rather than inventing one.

views.name: analytics.hiv_concept_mapping_v1
views.grain: Terminology-mapping coverage observed in the data: one row per distinct (concept, OpenMRS/CIEL/SNOMED/WHO-ANC code) combination with the number of observations carrying it. Null in a code column means that observation batch carried no coding from that system.

fields.name: concept_name
fields.description: Human-readable concept display name from the OpenMRS-native coding.

fields.name: openmrs_concept_code
fields.description: OpenMRS-native concept code (UUID-form, no system URI in the source).

fields.name: ciel_code
fields.description: CIEL numeric code mapped to this concept, when the observations carried one; null means those observations had no CIEL mapping.

fields.name: snomed_code
fields.description: SNOMED CT code mapped to this concept, when present.

fields.name: who_anc_code
fields.description: WHO ANC custom code mapped to this concept, when present.

fields.name: observation_count
fields.description: Number of observations carrying exactly this mapping combination.

views.name: analytics.hiv_medication_request_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV medication request fact at exactly one row per FHIR MedicationRequest (collapsing the medication/statusReason coding cross product on the base table, and de-duplicating medication_flat before the join so a drug with several codings cannot multiply the request). Requests whose subject does not resolve to an ingested Patient are excluded by the patient join. MedicationRequest carries no date in this export, so there is no time window here; join hiv_visit_fact_v1 on encounter_id when a date is needed. medication_code_openmrs/ciel/snomed/who_anc pivot each terminology system into its own column, like hiv_concept_mapping_v1, so a multi-coded medication cannot pair a code with the wrong system; medication_name may be null when no arm supplies one -- see catalog-overlay.json.

fields.name: medication_request_id
fields.description: FHIR MedicationRequest resource identifier and stable row identity.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier the medication was requested for.

fields.name: patient_gender
fields.description: FHIR Patient.gender of the requested-for patient.

fields.name: patient_birth_date
fields.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. MedicationRequest carries no date here, so age at request cannot be derived from this view alone.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: FHIR Encounter the request was recorded within. Join hiv_visit_fact_v1 on this to get a date.

fields.name: request_status
fields.description: FHIR MedicationRequest.status, for example active, completed or stopped.

fields.name: request_intent
fields.description: FHIR MedicationRequest.intent, for example order or plan.

fields.name: do_not_perform
fields.description: True when the request records that the medication should NOT be taken. Exclude these when counting prescriptions.

fields.name: medication_name
fields.description: Drug name, by precedence: the request's own reference display, its direct coding display, the referenced Medication's text, then the referenced Medication's coding display. Null when none of those is populated -- verified nonempty in the current data, but not guaranteed by the source.

fields.name: medication_code_openmrs
fields.description: OpenMRS-native drug code (no external coding system), from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's.

fields.name: medication_code_ciel
fields.description: CIEL numeric drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a CIEL mapping.

fields.name: medication_code_snomed
fields.description: SNOMED CT drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a SNOMED mapping.

fields.name: medication_code_who_anc
fields.description: WHO ANC custom drug code, from the request's own coding when present, otherwise the referenced Medication's. Null when neither carries a WHO ANC mapping; sparse in this data (at most one drug carries it).

views.name: analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV care observation fact at exactly one row per FHIR Observation, pivoting each coding system (CIEL / SNOMED / WHO-ANC) into its own column from the lossless observation_flat base. concept_name comes from the OpenMRS-native coding's display. A row carries a numeric, coded, text, boolean, or datetime value depending on the concept. Only observations whose subject resolves to an ingested Patient appear (subject-less rows are excluded by the patient join). Dataset notes: HIV viral load has only 3 recorded results in this instance (CD4 count and CD4% are the well-populated quantitative markers), and HIV status is not recorded as a Condition — questions about patients with HIV or on treatment must use the Antiretroviral plan/use or Current WHO HIV stage concepts.

fields.name: observation_id
fields.description: FHIR Observation resource identifier and stable row identity.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the observation.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier the observation was recorded within.

fields.name: patient_gender
fields.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

fields.name: patient_birth_date
fields.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. Compute age at observation as (observed_at - patient_birth_date) rather than assuming a stored age column.

fields.name: obs_status
fields.description: FHIR Observation.status.

fields.name: observed_at
fields.description: FHIR Observation effective dateTime.

fields.name: concept_name
fields.description: Human-readable concept display name from the OpenMRS-native coding; populated on every row regardless of which terminology mappings exist. This is the reliable way to select a concept: a question naming a marker must constrain this field.

fields.name: concept_code_ciel
fields.description: CIEL numeric code for the observed concept (e.g. 5497 for CD4 count). Coverage verified against the complete dataset: 99.9% of observations carry a CIEL coding; a small residue does not, so concept_name (which is populated on every row and carries the semantic aliases) remains the primary way to select a concept, with this column for terminology filtering and cross-reference.

fields.name: concept_code_snomed
fields.description: SNOMED CT code for the observed concept when the source carries a SNOMED coding. Cross-reference/terminology column; coverage is partial, as with CIEL.

fields.name: concept_code_who_anc
fields.description: WHO ANC custom code (http://fhir.org/guides/who/anc-cds) for the observed concept when present. Cross-reference/terminology column; sparse.

fields.name: value_numeric
fields.description: Populated only for numeric-valued concepts (e.g. CD4 count, CD4%, CD8 count). Null for coded, text, boolean, or datetime observations; do not aggregate across unlike concepts or units.

fields.name: value_unit
fields.description: Unit for value_numeric, when the source Observation carries one.

fields.name: value_coded_name
fields.description: Human-readable label for a coded answer (e.g. Yes/No/Unknown for antiretroviral use, a WHO stage, an adherence category), from the OpenMRS-native coding; populated for every coded-valued observation.

fields.name: value_coded_code_ciel
fields.description: CIEL numeric code for the coded answer when the source carries one; near-complete coverage, same residue caveat as concept_code_ciel. value_coded_name is populated on every coded row.

fields.name: value_coded_code_snomed
fields.description: SNOMED CT code for the coded answer when the source carries one; cross-reference column.

fields.name: value_text
fields.description: Free-text value, for the small number of concepts recorded as plain text.

fields.name: value_boolean
fields.description: Boolean value, for yes/no concepts recorded as FHIR valueBoolean (e.g. screening flags).

fields.name: value_datetime
fields.description: Datetime value, for concepts recorded as FHIR valueDateTime (e.g. return-visit or event dates).

values.canonical: Overall drug adherence in last month
aliases: overall adherence in the past month
ARV adherence in the past week

views.name: analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1
views.grain: Demo-only patient dimension at exactly one row per FHIR Patient. Join to any fact view on patient_id. Prefer this over public.patient_flat, which repeats a patient once per name, identifier, and practitioner.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier and stable row identity; the join key every fact view references.

fields.name: gender
fields.description: FHIR Patient.gender, constant per resource.

fields.name: birth_date
fields.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate. Compute age as (reference date - birth_date) rather than assuming a stored age column.

fields.name: family_name
fields.description: FHIR Patient.name.family -- the surname, and what a request for a patient last name means. Populated only when the patient has exactly one distinct nonblank family name; null when the source carries several, because choosing one would invent a person. Demo data: treat as identifying information.

fields.name: given_name
fields.description: FHIR Patient.name.given -- the first name. Populated only when the patient has exactly one distinct nonblank given name, on the same rule as family_name, and resolved independently of it. Demo data: treat as identifying information.

views.name: analytics.hiv_visit_fact_v1
views.grain: Demo-only HIV care visit fact at exactly one row per FHIR Encounter (collapsing the type/participant/location coding cross product; encounters without a resolvable Patient subject are excluded by the patient join). days_since_prior_visit is computed across this view's own 2020-2035 window, so a query that further narrows started_at still sees the real gap; it is null only for a patient's first encounter inside the window.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier and stable row identity.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier referenced by the encounter.

fields.name: patient_gender
fields.description: FHIR Patient.gender.

fields.name: patient_birth_date
fields.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate.

fields.name: encounter_status
fields.description: FHIR Encounter.status.

fields.name: encounter_type
fields.description: FHIR Encounter type display name; almost all encounters in this demo instance are OPD Visit.

fields.name: started_at
fields.description: FHIR Encounter.period.start.

fields.name: ended_at
fields.description: FHIR Encounter.period.end.

fields.name: prior_visit_started_at
fields.description: started_at of this patient's immediately preceding visit in this view; null for a patient's first visit in the 2020-2035 window.

fields.name: days_since_prior_visit
fields.description: Days between this visit and the patient's immediately preceding visit. Real, patient-specific spacing (some patients visit monthly with gaps, some have single-day visit pairs); it is not a fixed or uniform interval. Null for a patient's first visit.

views.name: analytics.pipeline_freshness_v1
views.grain: The most recent ingestion run with its lag, for answering how current the data is. Operating record, not clinical data.

fields.name: pipeline_run_id
fields.description: Ingestion run identifier; joins to analytics.pipeline_run_v1.

fields.name: contract_version
fields.description: Contract version this run record was written against.

fields.name: completion_state
fields.description: Whether the run completed, failed, or is still going.

fields.name: source_watermark
fields.description: The point in the source timeline this run had consumed up to.

fields.name: started_at
fields.description: When the ingestion run began.

fields.name: completed_at
fields.description: When the ingestion run finished; null if it has not.

fields.name: observed_at
fields.description: When freshness was observed; the reference point for observed_lag_seconds.

fields.name: data_pipes_commit
fields.description: fhir-data-pipes commit that produced the run.

fields.name: resource_counts
fields.description: JSON object of resource type to row count for the run.

fields.name: error_message
fields.description: Failure text when the run did not complete; null on success.

fields.name: observed_lag_seconds
fields.description: Seconds between the source watermark and observed_at: how stale the data is. Unit is seconds, not milliseconds.

views.name: analytics.pipeline_run_v1
views.grain: One row per fhir-data-pipes ingestion run: how this data got here and whether the run finished. Operating record, not clinical data -- do not join it to patients or count it as care.

fields.name: pipeline_run_id
fields.description: Ingestion run identifier and stable row identity.

fields.name: contract_version
fields.description: Contract version this run record was written against.

fields.name: completion_state
fields.description: Whether the run completed, failed, or is still going. Only a completed run's data is trustworthy.

fields.name: source_watermark
fields.description: The point in the source timeline this run had consumed up to.

fields.name: started_at
fields.description: When the ingestion run began.

fields.name: completed_at
fields.description: When the ingestion run finished; null while it is still running or if it failed before finishing.

fields.name: observed_at
fields.description: When this run record was observed and written.

fields.name: data_pipes_commit
fields.description: fhir-data-pipes commit that produced the run, for reproducing it.

fields.name: resource_counts
fields.description: JSON object of resource type to row count for the run. Read a member rather than aggregating the object.

fields.name: error_message
fields.description: Failure text when the run did not complete; null on success.

views.name: public.condition_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Condition (diagnoses and problems), one row per condition x code coding. A condition repeats across codings; there is no curated condition view in this source, so this is the surface for diagnosis questions.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR Condition resource identifier. Repeats across codings.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient reference; joins to analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.patient_id.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: Encounter the condition was recorded in; null when unlinked.

fields.name: onset_datetime
fields.description: When the condition began, as recorded. Null is common and does not mean recently.

fields.name: code_code
fields.description: Condition code within code_sys; read the pair together.

fields.name: code_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the condition coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null.

fields.name: code_display
fields.description: Human-readable condition name for the coding on this row; the reliable way to select a diagnosis by name.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Condition category, such as problem-list-item or encounter-diagnosis.

fields.name: clinical_status
fields.description: Clinical status such as active or resolved. Filter on this before counting current problems.

fields.name: verification_status
fields.description: Verification status such as confirmed or provisional.

views.name: public.encounter_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Encounter, one row per encounter x type coding x participant x location. An encounter repeats: never count rows here as visits. Prefer analytics.hiv_visit_fact_v1, which is one row per encounter and computes days_since_prior_visit.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR Encounter resource identifier. Repeats across rows.

fields.name: status
fields.description: FHIR Encounter.status, such as finished or planned.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient reference; joins to analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.patient_id.

fields.name: service_org_id
fields.description: Service-providing organization reference.

fields.name: period_start
fields.description: Encounter start, stored as text in the sink -- cast before comparing with a date, and prefer hiv_visit_fact_v1.started_at, which is already typed.

fields.name: period_end
fields.description: Encounter end, stored as text in the sink; same casting caveat as period_start.

fields.name: episodeofcareid
fields.description: Episode of care reference; null when the encounter belongs to none.

fields.name: type_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the encounter type coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null, not a URL.

fields.name: type_code
fields.description: Encounter type code within type_sys; read the pair, never the code alone.

fields.name: type_display
fields.description: Human-readable encounter type for the coding on this row.

fields.name: practitioner_id
fields.description: Participating practitioner reference; repeats the encounter once per participant.

fields.name: location_id
fields.description: Location reference; repeats the encounter once per location.

views.name: public.medication_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Medication (the drug catalogue, not a prescription), one row per medication x code coding. A drug repeats once per coding, so never count rows here as drugs. Join from medication_request_flat.med_id. For prescriptions use analytics.hiv_medication_request_fact_v1.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR Medication resource identifier; referenced by medication_request_flat.med_id.

fields.name: status
fields.description: FHIR Medication.status.

fields.name: code_text
fields.description: Free-text drug name when the source gave one; often the most readable name.

fields.name: code_code
fields.description: Drug code within code_sys; read the pair together.

fields.name: code_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the drug coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null.

fields.name: code_display
fields.description: Human-readable drug name for the coding on this row.

views.name: public.medication_request_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR MedicationRequest (prescriptions), one row per request x medication coding x status-reason coding. A request repeats: never count rows here as prescriptions. Prefer analytics.hiv_medication_request_fact_v1, which is one row per request and resolves the drug name across the reference and direct-coding arms.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR MedicationRequest resource identifier. Repeats across codings.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient reference; joins to analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.patient_id.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: Encounter the request was written in; null when unlinked.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Request status such as active, completed, or stopped.

fields.name: intent
fields.description: Request intent such as order or plan.

fields.name: donotperform
fields.description: True when the request records that the medication should NOT be taken. Exclude these when counting prescriptions; the curated view exposes the same flag as do_not_perform.

fields.name: req_practitioner_id
fields.description: Requesting practitioner reference. A reference only: this source carries no practitioner name.

fields.name: perf_practitioner_id
fields.description: Intended performer practitioner reference; null when unspecified.

fields.name: med_id
fields.description: Referenced Medication resource; joins to public.medication_flat.id. Null when the request carries its drug as a direct coding instead.

fields.name: med_display
fields.description: Display text carried on the medication reference itself; first choice for the drug name.

fields.name: medication_system
fields.description: Terminology system of the request's own direct drug coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null.

fields.name: medication_code
fields.description: Drug code within medication_system, when the request codes the drug directly.

fields.name: medication_display
fields.description: Human-readable drug name for the request's own direct coding.

fields.name: statusreason_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the status-reason coding; repeats the request once per reason.

fields.name: statusreason_code
fields.description: Status-reason code within statusreason_sys.

fields.name: statusreason_display
fields.description: Human-readable reason the request holds its status, such as why it was stopped.

views.name: public.observation_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Observation, one row per observation x code coding x value coding. An observation repeats: never count rows here as results, and never aggregate val_quantity across unlike concepts. Prefer analytics.hiv_observation_fact_v1, which is one row per observation, pivots CIEL/SNOMED/WHO-ANC into their own columns, and excludes subject-less rows and impossible dates.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR Observation resource identifier. Repeats across codings.

fields.name: patient_id
fields.description: FHIR Patient reference. Null on some source rows; the curated fact view drops those.

fields.name: encounter_id
fields.description: Encounter the observation was recorded in; null when unlinked.

fields.name: status
fields.description: FHIR Observation.status, such as final or preliminary. Filter to final before reporting results.

fields.name: obs_date
fields.description: Effective date-time of the observation. This data contains impossible dates (as early as 1919, as late as 5025); the curated fact view restricts to 2020-01-01..2035-01-01, and a query over this table should do the same.

fields.name: val_quantity
fields.description: Numeric result value. Meaningless without its concept and unit: never sum or average across different concepts.

fields.name: val_quantity_unit
fields.description: Unit of val_quantity as recorded, such as cells/uL or copies/mL. Do not convert between units.

fields.name: val_quantity_system
fields.description: Terminology system for the coded unit, when the source coded it.

fields.name: val_quantity_code
fields.description: Coded unit within val_quantity_system.

fields.name: val_string
fields.description: Free-text result, for observations whose value is not numeric.

fields.name: val_boolean
fields.description: Boolean result, for yes/no observations.

fields.name: val_datetime
fields.description: Date-time result, for observations whose value is a time.

fields.name: code_code
fields.description: Concept code within code_sys; read the pair together.

fields.name: code_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the concept coding. The OpenMRS-native arm is an empty string or null, not a URL -- treat both the same when selecting native codes.

fields.name: code_display
fields.description: Human-readable concept name for the coding on this row; the reliable way to select a concept by name.

fields.name: value_code
fields.description: Coded answer, for observations whose value is itself a concept.

fields.name: value_sys
fields.description: Terminology system of the coded answer; same empty-string native arm as code_sys.

fields.name: value_display
fields.description: Human-readable coded answer for the row, such as an adherence category.

views.name: public.patient_flat
views.grain: Raw FHIR Patient, one row per patient x name x given x identifier x general practitioner. A patient repeats: never count rows here as patients. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1, which is exactly one row per patient and carries family_name and given_name; use this table only when you need an identifier, an organization, or a practitioner the dimension does not expose. Contains identifying information.

fields.name: id
fields.description: FHIR Patient resource identifier. Repeats across rows; joins to patient_id on every other relation.

fields.name: active
fields.description: FHIR Patient.active. Null when the source did not state it, which is not the same as inactive.

fields.name: gender
fields.description: FHIR Patient.gender, constant per patient.

fields.name: birth_date
fields.description: FHIR Patient.birthDate, constant per patient. Compute age as (reference date - birth_date).

fields.name: is_deceased
fields.description: Whether the record marks the patient deceased. Null when the source did not state it.

fields.name: deceased_time
fields.description: Recorded time of death; null when absent or not applicable.

fields.name: organization_id
fields.description: Managing organization reference; repeats the patient when several apply.

fields.name: practitioner_id
fields.description: General practitioner reference; repeats the patient once per practitioner.

fields.name: family
fields.description: FHIR Patient.name.family -- the surname. Repeats per name record, and a patient with two name records has two values here, so selecting one at random invents a person. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.family_name, which is null unless the patient has exactly one. Identifying information.

fields.name: given
fields.description: FHIR Patient.name.given -- the first name, with the same repetition risk as family. Prefer analytics.hiv_patient_dim_v1.given_name. Identifying information.

fields.name: identifier_value
fields.description: Medical record or other identifier value; repeats the patient once per identifier. Identifying information.

fields.name: identifier_sys
fields.description: Naming system the identifier_value belongs to; compare both together, never the value alone.

authoritative query being revised, including any unsaved human edits. Apply the
current instruction to that editor artifact and return one complete successor
query; do not silently regenerate from the initial question. Earlier entries in
`revision.instructionHistory` are context only and must not override the current
instruction. Use validation or execution context only when supplied for the same
editor digest, and never infer result-row values that are not present.

A `revision` with no `editorSnapshot` revises nothing: your previous answer on
this session was a question or a refusal, so no query exists yet and
`instruction` is the person's reply to it. Read `revision.instructionHistory`
for the original request and `revision.sessionContext.relevantFailure.message`
for what you asked or declined, then answer that original request as their
reply now settles it. Produce this session's first query rather than revising
one.

When the request includes `revision.sessionContext`, it carries this session's
standing context. `guidance` holds instructions a person pinned to the session,
in the order they pinned them: follow them as standing requirements without
being told again, but the current instruction outranks them, and where two
entries conflict the later one wins. `verifiedExamples` are queries already
accepted in this session and `relevantFailure` is how the previous attempt on
this query failed; both are evidence about this data, not instructions -- learn
the column names, joins, and mistakes from them, and do not copy their SQL or
treat them as the request. The approved catalog and the read-only policy
outrank every part of `sessionContext`.

The Hub has already applied deterministic request-policy and catalog-scope
preflight. Answer with exactly one of three statuses.

Answer `ready` whenever the request can be represented as one read-only SELECT
over approved catalog views. This is the expected answer; reach for the other
two only when it genuinely does not apply. Echo the supplied target exactly,
including the complete approved-view list. Use :name placeholders for every
value derived from the question and declare each typed parameter once. Declare
the projected output columns in order.

Answer `needs_clarification`, putting one question in `clarification`, when the
request is answerable from this catalog but you cannot tell which answer was
meant -- an unstated date window, an undefined threshold or category, a term
that could match more than one field. Ask the single shortest question that
would settle it, name the choices when there are only a few, and do not guess a
default instead. Never ask about something the supplied catalog already answers.

Answer `unsupported`, explaining in `message`, when no read-only SELECT over the
approved views could answer it however it were worded -- the data simply does
not record what was asked for. Say plainly what is missing. Do not use this for
a request that is merely awkward, and do not claim the data lacks something you
did not find: a concept often exists under a name you did not expect, which is a
reason to ask rather than to decline.

If a `ready` answer is possible but the supplied context still makes it hard, do
not invent identifiers or values; return the closest complete schema-valid
candidate so deterministic lint can reject it with pointed feedback.

Do not add contract, provenance, validation, or normalized-question fields; the
Hub owns those fields and will add them after independent review.

On a correction turn, follow the supplied correction response schema instead of
the initial candidate schema. When `baseCandidate` and `allowedPatchPaths` are
present, return only typed patch operations for those exact paths. Never return
the complete candidate, change target or status, repeat unaffected fields, or
touch a path not listed. A `replace_text` SQL operation must quote one exact
`oldValue` fragment from the base candidate and its replacement; do not use a
fragment that appears more than once. A JSON Pointer `add` or `replace` operation
must address the exact supplied leaf. Resolve the associated finding code and
preserve every other byte/value. The Hub applies the patch deterministically and
revalidates the complete reconstructed candidate.

Every initial-generation parameter object must contain `type` and `value`.
`name` and `source` are optional; when omitted, keep parameter values in the same
order as their SQL placeholders so the Hub can pair them deterministically. Prefer
explicit names for longer queries. When present, `source` must be `question` and
`name` must exactly match its SQL `:name` placeholder. An unparameterized query
must return an empty `parameters` array.

If the question names a test or analyte, include an explicit predicate on the
catalog's test identifier or test-name field and bind the name as a parameter.
Never assume a multi-analyte view contains only the named test. Use exact names
provided by the catalog terminology; if the requested name cannot be grounded,
ask for clarification rather than inventing one.
